name: EchoGuard 4D radar (Echodyne)
description: K-band MESA ESA panel, 120 x 80 deg field of view, 6 km instrumented. Datasheet: sUAV over 1 km (Phantom 4), over 1.4 km (Matrice 600), vehicle 3.5 km. Up to 20 tracks at 10 Hz.

elevationDeg.condition: elevation field of view — Datasheet gives an 80 deg elevation SPAN only. Splitting it symmetrically about boresight is INFERRED, matching how lib-echoshield already models a 90 deg span as [-45,45].

rangeAccuracyM.condition: range accuracy <3.25 m (vendor bound taken as 1 sigma)
rangeAccuracyM.source: Echodyne EchoGuard product page and spec sheet (25JA1)

azimuthAccuracyDeg.condition: track accuracy <1° azimuth; precision tracking <0.5° (vendor bound taken as 1 sigma)
azimuthAccuracyDeg.source: Echodyne EchoGuard product page and spec sheet (25JA1)

elevationAccuracyDeg.condition: track accuracy <1.5° elevation; precision tracking <0.5° (vendor bound taken as 1 sigma)
elevationAccuracyDeg.source: Echodyne EchoGuard product page and spec sheet (25JA1)

falseAlarmRatePerScan.note: Planning factor: PLACARD_PFA 1e-6 (src/model/types.ts) times about 1e6 range-azimuth-Doppler cells per scan of a 360° surveillance volume gives about one false alarm per scan over the whole coverage; this 120° sector panel searches about half the cells and is recorded at 0.5. No vendor publishes a false-alarm rate.

dwellTimeS.note: Planning factor: Echodyne publishes no dwell or CPI. An electronically scanned radar sets its dwell in the beam schedule rather than by beamwidth over scan rate; the literature CPI of 20 ms for X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs is used. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. The EchoGuard spec sheet (6JL) gives a 10 Hz track update and "thousands of pencil-thin beams ... in milliseconds" but no dwell.

pulsesPerDwell.note: Planning factor: Echodyne publishes no PRF or pulse count. 20 ms dwell at the literature 5 kHz PRF gives 100 pulses coherently integrated. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. The EchoGuard spec sheet (6JL) gives a 10 Hz track update and "thousands of pencil-thin beams ... in milliseconds" but no dwell.
